skill.name: frontend-fundamentals

skill.summary: Review frontend components for architecture, state management, performance, accessibility, and maintainability.

content.value_statement: Frontend reviews often miss architecture, state, accessibility, and performance issues until components become hard to maintain. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused checklist questions and review patterns for component quality.
actual_capabilities: Reviews React, Vue, and Svelte component code for maintainability concerns.
Checks component responsibility, file size, prop count, and naming clarity.
Evaluates state location, prop drilling, context usage, and server state separation.
Flags performance risks involving memoization, callbacks, re-renders, and lazy loading.
Prompts accessibility checks for semantic HTML, ARIA usage, and keyboard navigation.
Provides Socratic questions that help junior developers reason through frontend decisions.
limitations: Does not run tests, lint commands, or browser checks by itself.
Does not provide framework-specific configuration files or automated fixes.
Relies on the reviewer to provide relevant component code and project context.
References a standards document path that is not included in this skill package.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request
use_cases.description: Apply a structured checklist before merging frontend component changes.

use_cases.title: Coach component design
use_cases.description: Use guided questions to help a developer identify splitting, state, and naming issues.

use_cases.title: Audit UI maintainability
use_cases.description: Assess a component set for repeated patterns that increase complexity and review cost.

prompt_templates.title: Basic component review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this frontend component with the frontend-fundamentals checklist. Focus on one responsibility, prop count, and accessibility.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single component

prompt_templates.title: State placement review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these related components for state management. Identify which state should stay local, move upward, or use server state tools.

prompt_templates.title: Performance and accessibility pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this UI change for avoidable re-renders, heavy rendering work, lazy loading opportunities, semantic HTML, and keyboard access.

prompt_templates.title: Mentor-style review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request as a mentor. Ask Socratic questions first, then list the highest-impact frontend architecture changes.

output_examples.input: A dashboard component handles data loading, routing decisions, state updates, and all presentation.
output_examples.output: The review would recommend splitting the container responsibilities from smaller presentation components and extracting the data loading logic.

output_examples.input: A component passes the same user object through four nested layers to one widget.
output_examples.output: The review would flag prop drilling and ask whether a closer data source or shared context would make the dependency clearer.

output_examples.input: A list view filters items during every render and uses generic containers for interactive controls.
output_examples.output: The review would suggest memoizing expensive derived values and replacing nonsemantic interactive elements with accessible controls.

best_practices: Provide the complete component and nearby callers so the review can judge responsibility boundaries.
Ask for the highest-impact findings first when reviewing large pull requests.
Pair checklist results with project conventions before requesting code changes.
anti_patterns: Using the checklist as a rigid rule without considering product context.
Requesting broad reviews without sharing the component code or user flow.
Treating performance suggestions as required before measuring real impact.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers React, Vue, and Svelte component reviews, plus general frontend rendering and styling concerns.

faq.question: Does it automatically modify code?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance, questions, and recommendations for the assistant to apply.

faq.question: Can it replace accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No. It helps reviewers notice accessibility risks, but browser testing and assistive technology checks are still needed.

faq.question: Is it useful for junior developer mentoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Socratic questions designed to guide learning without immediately giving answers.

faq.question: Does it include external tooling?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown review guide and does not run commands or install packages.

faq.question: What code quality problems does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes large components, unclear responsibilities, prop drilling, render logic, accessibility gaps, and unnecessary re-renders.
